approaches.name: Self-attention
approaches.problem: Each token needs information from other tokens in the same sequence.
approaches.how_it_works: Compute query, key, and value vectors, use query-key matches to weight value vectors, and mix the information back into each token.
approaches.why_it_matters: It lets the model build context-sensitive token meanings instead of reading with one narrow memory.
approaches.failure_mode: Attention can be expensive for long contexts and can focus on misleading tokens.

approaches.name: Transformer block stacking
approaches.problem: One attention pass is not enough to build rich language representations.
approaches.how_it_works: Repeat attention, feed-forward updates, residual paths, and normalization across many layers so each layer refines the token vectors produced by earlier layers.
approaches.why_it_matters: Stacking lets later layers build more abstract features from earlier token relations.
approaches.failure_mode: Deep stacks become unstable or expensive without careful normalization and residual design.

approaches.name: Positional encoding
approaches.problem: Plain attention does not know token order.
approaches.how_it_works: Add or combine position information with token embeddings before attention layers process them.
approaches.why_it_matters: It lets the model distinguish sequences with the same words in different orders.
approaches.failure_mode: Poor position handling can break long-context behavior or confuse order-sensitive tasks.

approaches.name: Causal masking
approaches.problem: A next-token model must not see future answer tokens during training.
approaches.how_it_works: Block attention from each token to later tokens by masking future attention scores.
approaches.why_it_matters: It keeps the training task honest and matches generation, where future tokens are unknown.
approaches.failure_mode: Wrong masks leak answers or prevent the model from using valid context.

approaches.name: Next-token pretraining
approaches.problem: The model needs a broad signal that can be created from raw text at scale.
approaches.how_it_works: Train the model to predict the next token from previous context across a very large corpus.
approaches.why_it_matters: Good prediction forces the model to learn grammar, facts, style, code patterns, and common reasoning habits.
approaches.failure_mode: Predicting likely text can produce fluent falsehoods and does not guarantee helpful behavior.

approaches.name: Token-to-logit pipeline
approaches.problem: Text must become model input and model output in a computable form.
approaches.how_it_works: Tokenize text, embed token ids, process vectors through transformer blocks, and project final vectors to vocabulary logits.
approaches.why_it_matters: It is the basic mechanism behind modern LLM training and generation.
approaches.failure_mode: Tokenizer choices, context limits, or bad probability calibration can damage output quality.

approaches.name: Large-scale pretraining system
approaches.problem: A useful LLM requires huge amounts of data and compute without unstable optimization.
approaches.how_it_works: Feed curated token batches through the model, compute cross-entropy loss, backpropagate gradients, and validate on held-out data.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns the simple prediction task into a reliable training process at scale.
approaches.failure_mode: Bad data, bad schedules, duplicates, or poor validation can waste compute or teach bad behavior.

approaches.name: Efficient scaling
approaches.problem: More capability usually costs more training and inference compute.
approaches.how_it_works: Use scaling choices, routing, or sparse activation so capacity grows without activating every parameter for every token.
approaches.why_it_matters: It makes larger models more practical to train or serve.
approaches.failure_mode: Efficiency tricks can add routing errors, uneven expert use, or difficult system complexity.

approaches.name: Supervised fine-tuning
approaches.problem: A pretrained model may not answer in the desired format or style.
approaches.how_it_works: Train on prompt-response examples that demonstrate the wanted behavior, so the model learns how instructions should map to complete answers.
approaches.why_it_matters: It teaches instruction following more directly than raw next-token pretraining.
approaches.failure_mode: The model can overfit the examples or inherit narrow demonstration habits.

approaches.name: Preference tuning
approaches.problem: Many answer qualities are easier to compare than to write as exact labels.
approaches.how_it_works: Collect chosen/rejected answer pairs and update the model through a reward model, RL objective, or direct preference loss.
approaches.why_it_matters: It moves the model toward answers people judge better after it already knows language.
approaches.failure_mode: The preference signal can reward style over truth or be gamed by the model.

approaches.name: Reasoning traces
approaches.problem: A final answer does not show the intermediate choices that produced it.
approaches.how_it_works: Let the model generate intermediate written steps and use those steps as context before the final answer.
approaches.why_it_matters: It gives the model a workspace for multi-step tasks and exposes partial work for checking.
approaches.failure_mode: The trace can be long, fluent, and still wrong or unnecessary.

approaches.name: Verifier-guided reasoning
approaches.problem: The model needs feedback about which attempted solutions are likely correct.
approaches.how_it_works: Sample candidate traces or answers, score them with a verifier or final check, and train or select using that score.
approaches.why_it_matters: It can improve hard tasks where one sample is unreliable.
approaches.failure_mode: A weak verifier can reward shortcuts, superficial correctness, or overfit solution styles.

approaches.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
approaches.problem: The model weights may not contain current, private, or exact information.
approaches.how_it_works: Embed the query and documents, retrieve relevant chunks, and place them into the model context before answering.
approaches.why_it_matters: It gives the model grounded information without retraining the whole model.
approaches.failure_mode: Bad retrieval or prompt injection can make the answer worse than using no retrieval.

approaches.name: Tool-calling agent loop
approaches.problem: Some tasks require actions outside text generation.
approaches.how_it_works: Let the model choose structured tool calls, execute them, feed observations back, and repeat until done.
approaches.why_it_matters: It lets the system calculate, search, code, inspect, and update state.
approaches.failure_mode: The loop can call the wrong tool, trust bad outputs, leak data, or fail to stop.

approaches.name: Task-specific evaluation
approaches.problem: A general benchmark may not measure the behavior a real use case needs.
approaches.how_it_works: Define target tasks and failure modes, then measure accuracy, usefulness, safety, cost, and latency on those slices.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns evaluation into evidence for a concrete deployment rather than a vanity score.
approaches.failure_mode: Bad slices or contaminated benchmarks can hide real regressions.

approaches.name: Human and preference evaluation
approaches.problem: Some answer qualities are subjective or hard to capture with rules.
approaches.how_it_works: Ask people or preference models to compare outputs on clarity, helpfulness, correctness, and policy fit.
approaches.why_it_matters: It captures aspects of user experience that automatic metrics miss.
approaches.failure_mode: Judgments can be noisy, biased, expensive, and sensitive to rubric wording.

approaches.name: Pipeline-based paper reading
approaches.problem: New LLM papers can look unrelated because each names a different component.
approaches.how_it_works: Locate the method in the pipeline: tokens, embeddings, attention, training objective, tuning, retrieval, tools, reasoning, or evaluation.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns new trends into understandable modifications of known parts.
approaches.failure_mode: A method can change several parts at once, so oversimplifying the location can miss the real tradeoff.

approaches.name: Bottleneck-first analysis
approaches.problem: Trends are hard to judge if they are read only as names or demos.
approaches.how_it_works: Ask what bottleneck the method attacks, what object it introduces, and what failure mode remains.
approaches.why_it_matters: It keeps attention on mechanism and tradeoff instead of hype.
approaches.failure_mode: The stated bottleneck may differ from the real deployment bottleneck.
